captures.description: THE FOUNDATION, SIGNED OUT, 2026-11-01: 'Common Crawl is a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization founded in 2007 by Gil Elbaz that collects, preserves, and freely shares an open archive of internet data.' Core details and scale (mission; 'over 10 to 11 petabytes of data spanning nearly two decades'; 3 to 5 billion new pages a month; AWS hosting at s3://commoncrawl); data formats (WARC, WET, WAT); use cases and controversies (training for models 'developed by companies like OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, and Meta'; over 10,000 papers; CCBot and paywalls); an offer on querying the index for a URL or blocking CCBot. Eleven cards: Common Crawl (two), Wikipedia, The Atlantic, the Registry of Open Data on AWS, LinkedIn, DEV Community, three videos, InfluenceWatch.

atoms.evidence: Common Crawl is a 501(c)(3) non-profit organization founded in 2007 by Gil Elbaz
that collects, preserves, and freely shares an open archive of internet data.
Adds roughly 3 to 5 billion new web pages each month.
Mission: To democratize access to web information for researchers, educators, and developers.
Hosting: Stored for free on Amazon Web Services (AWS) via its Open Data Sponsorship Program
